title: Fleet Replica Sync Health on G1-M05
description: Verify and restore the fleet replica sync of the shared worktree C:\semio on Windows workstation g1-m05: scheduled task semio-fleet-replica, beat.json/health.json freshness, head.json publication, inbound changes from other origins, errors/backlog in C:\semio\.cache\f. Fix root-cause defects. Report with timestamps.
summary: g1-m05 replica caught up fully (0 origins behind). The daemon runs at AboveNormal. Before anything inbound was applied, a sha-manifested backup of the 1,321 locally differing files went to C:\b\semio-local-20261123. Lost copies were reconciled with three-way merges against the frozen-view base (last fleet put before min(mtime, 2026-11-22T11:15:43Z)). An earlier nearest-ancestor merge had reverted fleet work in 13 files; each was restored to the exact fleet bytes and merged again correctly. All 31 merged or restored files are published fleet-wide (published-check.mjs). Local work superseded by the fleet stays in .cache/f/lost and is listed in the report. Own fixes (sidecar priority, journal replaceFile) were re-merged onto the newer fleet versions; pass-reuse went back to the fleet design.

interactions.author: ueli
interactions.summary: Replica on g1-m05 was down ~15 h (head unpublished since 08:53, inbound stopped ~12:15). The watchdog killed the daemon in a loop: CPU starvation at Task Scheduler priority 7. Fixed: the replica now applies its declared interactive class itself (verified AboveNormal live, lag 15 s → <200 ms). The own-origin writer moves aside a file that refuses replacement (the attest.json EPERM on NFS for 19 h, unstuck). Tests added. Still broken at close: host memory thrash from 3×10–11 GB link.exe (FEM build) stalls the daemon. It should recover once the linkers finish. Report: fleet-replica-sync-health-report.md.

interactions.prompt: Fix everything and get this worker in sync again, without losing local changes and without overwriting other agents' changes.
